subsystem.name: GenericRuntimeObjects
subsystem.responsibility: Heterogeneous collection of small runtime-object helpers on the generic runtime path: no-op stubs (nullsubs), constant-return stubs, byte-field accumulator helpers, offset/sub-object accessors, a guarded string-copy setter, a path filename-extraction utility, and one NetComm session-peer slot setter. The grouping follows the wave_008_generic_runtime_objects scope; shared module provenance is not established by this packet.

summary: This packet is a grab-bag of 77 small runtime helpers. 62 are empty no-op stubs (nullsub/NullStub/EmptyFunction) that return void immediately; three return fixed constants (0x00454D96 returns 1; 0x004579B0, 0x0047AA70, 0x0048B024 return 0); one is a pass-through identity (0x00461CC3). A coherent byte-at-offset-94 accumulation pattern appears in four unrelated functions (0x0044F062, 0x004636E6, 0x0047E384, 0x00486EC8) whose object bases are not proven shared, so they are not merged. A small number of functions carry real behavior: the NetComm session-peer slot setter (0x0045E5D0, owner DERIVED from callers 0x0045D890/0x00460520), the path filename-extraction utility (0x004618D0, caller 0x00461610), two EntityVisibilityGridManager helpers (0x00464AE0 byte-range predicate and 0x00464F90 threshold-to-rank classifier, caller 0x00465460), the guarded string copy (0x004761A0, buffer at this+80), the single-call passthrough (0x00478E80, caller 0x004793EC, delegate FUN_00499b80), and three fixed-displacement offset accessors (0x00466B10, 0x0046B310, 0x0046B829). Two functions decompile to corrupted/empty bodies under flagged positive stack deltas (0x0047F006, 0x0046624E) and are treated as unknowable. The proposal deliberately keeps most owners as UnknownObject rather than inventing classes from bare offsets.

classes.name: NetCommSessionPeer
classes.responsibility: Per-peer session state in the NetComm session path; exposes a DWORD-array of per-index slots addressed through `this` by a peer/session index. Owner identity is DERIVED only from the two recorded callers (0x0045D890, 0x00460520); no layout evidence beyond the single write site exists. No field: evidence refs exist in this packet, so no class field is declared.

compatibility_contracts.name: FixedConstantReturns
compatibility_contracts.description: Constant-return stubs must keep returning their fixed values at their call sites: 0x00454D96 returns 1; 0x004579B0, 0x0047AA70, and 0x0048B024 return 0. A replacement must preserve these return values wherever the referencing call sites are retained.

compatibility_contracts.name: Byte94AccumulatorSemantics
compatibility_contracts.description: Four functions (0x0044F062, 0x004636E6, 0x0047E384, 0x00486EC8) accumulate a byte argument into the byte at offset 94 of an object pointer. They differ in return behavior: 0x0044F062 returns -1 while the others return the argument. A replacement preserving these call sites must keep the byte-at-offset-94 accumulation and each function's own return value.

compatibility_contracts.name: NetCommSessionPeerSlotSetter
compatibility_contracts.description: 0x0045E5D0 writes its value argument into DWORD-array slot this[a2 + 117] of the session-peer object and returns that value. Session code at 0x0045D890 and 0x00460520 depends on this write-and-return contract.

compatibility_contracts.name: PathFilenameExtraction
compatibility_contracts.description: 0x004618D0 returns a pointer past the last backslash of the input path string, or the string start when no backslash is present. SessionConfigBuilder (0x00461610) consumes the returned filename pointer.

compatibility_contracts.name: NoopStubRetention
compatibility_contracts.description: The nullsub stubs are observable only as no-op call targets. If any are referenced by vtable or call tables, a replacement must keep an equivalent no-op slot at those call sites or rewire the referencing tables; otherwise table semantics change.

compatibility_contracts.name: OffsetAccessorStability
compatibility_contracts.description: Offset accessors return fixed sub-object pointers relative to their object: 0x00466B10 returns this + 0x104, 0x0046B310 returns this + 0x174, 0x0046B829 returns this + 304. A replacement must preserve these layout displacements or rewire the call sites that consume them.

unresolved: Owners of the byte-at-offset-94 accumulator objects (0x0044F062, 0x004636E6, 0x0047E384, 0x00486EC8) are unidentified. The equal offset 0x5E is not merged into a single class because the packet does not prove common ownership of the four object bases.
Purpose and call sites of the no-op nullsub stubs are not evidenced; they cannot be distinguished as vtable placeholders, disabled callbacks, or dead-code-removal residue.

NetCommSessionPeer (0x0045E5D0) is DERIVED only from the two caller names (0x0045D890, 0x00460520); no field or class layout evidence beyond the single write site is present. The DWORD-array slot at this[a2 + 117] implies a per-peer slot whose byte offset (0x1D4 at index 0) cannot be confirmed; no field: evidence ref exists in the packet, so the slot is recorded here rather than as a class field.
ByteCounterIncrement (0x0044F062) carries a flagged positive stack adjustment; the userpurge parameter layout and the -1 return are MEDIUM trust and may be wrong.
CorruptedThunk_f006 (0x0047F006) and sub_46624E (0x0046624E) decompile to corrupted/empty bodies under a positive sp warning; their real behavior is unknowable from the raw source.
The sub-object types behind offset accessors 0x00466B10 (0x104), 0x0046B310 (0x174), and 0x0046B829 (304) are unknown.
StringCopyWithBufferRealloc (callee of 0x004761A0) and the object holding the string buffer at offset 80 are outside this packet; signature, allocation policy, and failure behavior are unresolved.
FUN_00499b80 (delegate of 0x00478E80) is a LEGACY ABI label with no prototype; delegate semantics are unresolved.
extractFilenameFromPath (0x004618D0) returns the string start when no backslash is present; whether that boundary behavior matches SessionConfigBuilder expectations is unconfirmed.
ThresholdToRankClassifier (0x00464F90) classifies by thresholds 1487/2975/7200/28800; the ranked quantity and the meaning of the five ranks are unknown.
The MK_FP(return-address) expressions in 0x00455258 and 0x0046C6E5 are decompiler artifacts of bare ret bodies, not genuine indirect calls.
ReturnTrueStub (0x00454D96) and ReturnZeroStub (0x004579B0) have no caller evidence; whether their fixed values are booleans, status codes, or enumeration constants is unresolved.
